history.period: Legend 18th century; present temple complex later (temple built using materials of an old Jain temple of Khed, per one source)
history.summary: Rani Bhatiyani (Majisa), born Swarup Kanwar, daughter of Jogidas Bhati of Jaisalmer, was married to Rao Kalyan Singh, the Mahecha Rathore chief of Jasol. After the death of her young son Lal Singh, she died (one account says of shock, another that she committed sati after a rumour -- spread by her husband to be rid of her -- that he had died in battle). She then appeared to two Manganiyar/Dholi devotees, and the Thakurs of Jasol built a shrine to her, since which she is worshipped as a benevolent goddess across western Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Sindh (Pakistan). This is the major temple at Jasol village in Pachpadra tehsil, near Balotra -- CSV town 'Barmer' must be corrected: the temple is NOT in Barmer city but about 4 km from Balotra railway station (~32 km from Barmer city, ~120 km from Jodhpur), and it is one of the most visited shrines of western Rajasthan. A second major Bhatiyani temple stands at Jakhan in Osian tehsil, Jodhpur district. District: Barmer (Jasol lies in the former Pachpadra tehsil, now in Balotra district since 2023 -- flagged).

name: Rani Bhatiyani Temple
town_description: Jasol is a historic village in Pachpadra tehsil near Balotra in western Rajasthan, on the banks of the dry Luni river; the temple lies on the Nakoda-Balotra road, about 4 km from Balotra railway station.
